instruction.pc: unconditionally advances by one byte after either handler branch

handler.quarterMaxHp: floor(gBattleMons[gBattlerAttacker].maxHP / 4), with a defensive zero-to-one fallback

success.moveDamage: quarterMaxHp, with the same defensive zero-to-one fallback

scriptRoutes.alreadyLive: jumpifstatus2 BS_ATTACKER, STATUS2_SUBSTITUTE, BattleScript_AlreadyHasSubstitute; setalreadystatusedmoveattempt, short pause, STRINGID_PKMNHASSUBSTITUTE, MoveEnd
scriptRoutes.handlerFailure: setsubstitute then chooser == B_MSG_SUBSTITUTE_FAILED: short pause, gSubstituteUsedStringIds[B_MSG_SUBSTITUTE_FAILED] = STRINGID_TOOWEAKFORSUBSTITUTE, MoveEnd
scriptRoutes.handlerSuccess: setsubstitute then chooser != B_MSG_SUBSTITUTE_FAILED: attackanimation, waitanimation, healthbarupdate BS_ATTACKER, datahpupdate BS_ATTACKER, gSubstituteUsedStringIds[B_MSG_SET_SUBSTITUTE] = STRINGID_PKMNMADESUBSTITUTE, MoveEnd
scriptRoutes.persistence: the handler sets attacker status2/substituteHP; MOVEEND_SUBSTITUTE clears STATUS2_SUBSTITUTE for each battler only when its substituteHP is zero

boundedRemainder: The manifest exposes active HP, max HP, PP, status2, RNG, controller state, party checksums, and framebuffer hashes. It does not expose gDisableStructs[].substituteHP, gBattleMoveDamage, gBattleCommunication[MULTISTRING_CHOOSER], gHitMarker, BattleScript PC, or decoded text. Source therefore pins the internal branch/mutation and message routing; the ROM captures prove two real controller-selected PP reductions, floor(155/4)=38 HP loss, persistence into the next action, and the live-substitute message framebuffer. This is evidence only and does not implement or register the opcode/effect.
